descriptionChirho: Metaphorical extension of 'nose' to denote anger or wrath, often as a divine attribute (חֲרוֹן אַף 'burning anger'), covering all inflected and prepositional forms expressing rage, fury, or indignation.
The literal anatomical sense referring to the nose, nostrils, or snout of a person or animal, including singular, dual, and construct forms with pronominal suffixes and prepositions.
The dual form אַפַּיִם used to denote the face or countenance, especially in expressions of prostration (נָפַל עַל אַפָּיו 'fell on his face') or facial appearance.
The dual form אַפַּיִם in the idiomatic expression אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם 'slow to anger' (lit. 'long of nostrils'), a key divine attribute describing patience and forbearance.
An idiomatic use of the dual form to mean 'double' or 'twofold', as in Isaiah 40:2 where Jerusalem receives double for her sins.
